record.what_it_does: Graph database; Aura API manages cloud instances, Query API runs Cypher over HTTP.
record.auth_notes: Aura API (api.neo4j.io) uses the OAuth2 client_credentials grant. You create a Client ID and Secret in the Aura console, then POST them to https://api.neo4j.io/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth (ID as username, secret as password). That returns a bearer token that lasts 1 hour. There is no authorization-code or consent flow, so each end user supplies their own client ID and secret. The data plane (the HTTP Query API) takes Basic auth with the database username and password, or a Bearer token issued by an SSO provider.
record.access_notes: The auth docs state that every tier can create Aura API credentials. Free accounts, and Pro trials without a billing method, are limited to 25 requests per minute. Pro with billing, Business Critical and VDC get 125 requests per minute. The v2beta1 billing endpoints are limited to 10 requests per day per organization. Some actions are likely restricted on Free, such as creating paid instance types; this was not verified per endpoint.
record.api_breadth_notes: Aura API v1 covers instances (create, list, get, update/resize, pause, resume, delete, overwrite), snapshots, tenants/projects and customer-managed keys. It also has v2beta1 organization billing endpoints for ledger and usage. A separate HTTP Query API runs Cypher transactions. The official spec page would not render, so I could not count the operations; I estimate about 20–40.
record.mcp_notes: The official Neo4j MCP server lives at github.com/neo4j/mcp (releases). It installs with `uvx neo4j-mcp-server` from PyPI or `brew install neo4j-mcp`, and also ships as a binary and as the Docker image mcp/neo4j. It runs over stdio (default) or HTTP, and connects to one Neo4j database to do schema exploration and Cypher. I found no vendor-hosted remote URL. Separately, the neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j servers, including an Aura manager, are Labs/community projects.
record.blocker_notes: There is no multi-user OAuth consent flow, so each user has to paste in an Aura client ID and secret (client_credentials). For data access, each user also has to supply a database URI plus a username and password or an SSO token. Rate limits on the free tier are low (25 requests per minute). The official OpenAPI spec could not be downloaded (api.neo4j.io/openapi.json returned 403), and no webhooks are documented.
